task:
Link reference definitions have three faults. Fix all of them. First, a definition that spans many lines takes quadratic time. With the default markdownit(), each of these inputs must render in under 5 seconds: - '[a]: /u "' + 'x '.repeat(300000) (a title that never closes) - '[a]: /u "' + 'x '.repeat(300000) + '"' (a title that closes at the very end) - '[' + 'a '.repeat(300000) (a label that never closes) Second, reference labels have no length limit. CommonMark allows at most 999 Unicode code points in a label, and a surrogate pair counts as one. A label over the limit must not define a reference. After md.parse('[' + 'a'.repeat(999) + ']: /url [' + 'b'.repeat(1000) + ']: /url', env), Object.keys(env.references) must be exactly ['A'.repeat(999)]. Third, a title that continues onto a later line is accepted even with no whitespace between the destination and the title. A title needs whitespace before it. md.render('- [ref]: "open close"') must return '
  • [ref]: <url>"open close"
', so the text stays a paragraph. A valid multi-line title must keep working: md.render('[ref]: "open close" [ref]') must return '

ref

'. Everything else must keep working, including the CommonMark spec tests.
accept: npm run --silent test:markdown-it && npm run --silent test:cmspec
